- A merge to main runs publish.yaml: unless only docs (`*.md`, `docs`, `LICENSE`) changed since the commit `:latest` was built from, it tests, then pushes `sprobot`, `sprobot-web`, `stickybot` and `threadbot` to `ghcr.io/espresso-aficionados/` for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, tagged `sha-<short>` and `:latest`, with build-provenance attestations. bonnet's podman-auto-update restarts each bot when its `:latest` moves, so a merge is a release.
- Four static Go binaries (`CGO_ENABLED=0`) on distroless static `:nonroot`. `github.com/disgoorg/disgo` (with `omit` and `snowflake`) is the Discord gateway and REST client of the three bots (`pkg/bot`, `pkg/botutil`, `pkg/stickybot`, `pkg/threadbot`): every event and command it decodes comes from Discord members, so it is untrusted input. `TestCacheFlagsClassified` (`pkg/bot`) fails when a disgo release adds a cache flag that `groupedcache.go` has not classified.
- `github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2` (`credentials`, `service/s3`) in `pkg/s3client` stores profiles, guild config and files downloaded from Discord attachments (size-limited there) in an S3-compatible bucket with `S3_KEY`/`S3_SECRET`; `github.com/hashicorp/golang-lru/v2` caches profiles there. `cmd/sprobot-web` serves those files and profile pages publicly.
- `github.com/sadbox/svc` provides each binary's `-healthcheck`. Secrets (Discord tokens, S3 keys, healthcheck URLs) arrive as plain environment values rendered on the host; no dependency talks to a secrets store.
